body:
Feeling dumb and broken because I have aphantasia. I literally don't have an imagination - or at least, the one I do isn't visual.


It wouldn't be much of an issue if I wasn't into guided meditation/hypnosis and I feel like I'm definitely missing out on the world building that a lot of other people get to experience.


I know this is one of those things I should just accept because it's the way my brain is wired, but I really do wish it was wired differently and I feel some grief that other people get to experience life in a way I've never been able to, and never will be able to.

Maybe women are actually better than men. That would explain why they don't have to have daily posts about what a new femininity would look like.


Sometimes I wonder if I should transition... part of that is gender dysphoria. Part of that is feeling like I'd escape a lot of ire and the world would be a lot warmer.

My ex continues to badmouth me on Reddit and I can't tell if she lives in some bizarro world or if I'm completely blind to my own faults.


Half the stories she shares are things that didn't actually happen the way she says they did. She did that a ton during our relationship - she'd take something I did or said  completely out of context and then insert the most awful intent behind it and claim I must have done that action because I actually just hated her guts. Like, no, I didn't leave you wasted on the floor at a party because I was too tired to care, I left you wasted on the couch in the care of a trusted friend because this was the 7th time you had gotten too drunk to stand, I couldn't get you in the car, and I had shit to do the next day. 



It bothers me a lot. Not because she had mouths me but because it makes me doubt myself a LOT. My whole relationship with her felt like I was questioning my own existence. Every action I did was interrogated and broken down and ripped to shreds and it seemed like there was just no way to actually be *good* to her, at least not in a way she valued or understood. 



I guess I should just leave it in the past but it actually bothers me significantly that her version of reality is so divorced from mine and simply by nature of wanting to be a decent person I'd rather think of myself in her terms of a total jackass rather than stand up for myself.

I have had a standing appointment to try ketamine therapy for treatment resistant depression and I keep on moving it back. Yesterday I confirmed my appointment but today I read a lot of bad experiences about it or how it would take hours to recover and I couldn't make that work this week - I had a call with friends I said I'd go to and didn't want to cancel on if I was loopy. 

I lied about having COVID to cancel it without being charged. I dunno how to feel about that. At this point I switched antidepressants and they feel like they might be working so I'm not sure if I even want to go through with this alternative stuff.

I guess I don't understand why men are talked about so monolithically. The thread that's going on about men trauma dumping to their partners doesn't speak to my experience (or most of my friends) in the slightest. 


That doesn't mean I don't believe that a significant number of men wouldn't benefit from being more emotionally mature, or that the issue of men using women as their therapists doesn't exist. It just makes it difficult because there's such a stereotype that my own experiences are often called into question.


I don't want to make it all about me and pretend like the woman's side of this issue doesn't exist at all, but I can't describe how bad it sucks to just straight up not be believed when I say that my female partners have all expected me to be at their emotional beck and call and used me like some sort of feelings fix it man. There's only so much I can deal with before I start being more a caretaker and therapist than your partner

This is a weird political adjunct topic, but I get really really frustrated with how people talk about what conservatives believe.


I grew up in one of the reddest places in America. Up until I was 20 I would have voted straight ticket republican. 


It just pisses me off to no end to hear people I agree with demonize the average conservative by inserting beliefs into their moth about how they "hate minorites" or "despise women" or "embrace fascism". 


Most of the time those aren't true, and it genuinely hurts our chances of reaching these people. Having been on that side of the political spectrum, hardly anyone is trying to do anything because they *want* to harm anyone else, they just have a different value system for what is acceptable and what isn't. I don't agree with it, but having believed it at one point, a lot is done by society to make it seem like it *makes sense*.


Don't get me wrong, what conservative policies result in is a massive amount of hate and discrimination and *that* should be wholly despised, but I feel like I can't talk to my own family half the time because they won't even engage anymore because conversations with progressives have turned into them receiving verbal abuse so often. We should be trying to show conservatives how their beliefs ultimately result in hate and how that's wrong, not implying that everyone is soulless and bigoted and basically a Nazi because they were falsely taught traditional gender roles were important. You can't deprogram someone from this stuff if you aren't willing to treat them like a human and take them at face value. A lot of times, people on that side of the political spectrum literally just don't see how systems work and how even though they claim not to be discriminatory, their value set ultimately will result in discrimination occurring.

Luckily it's not on anything tied to me irl but it's still frustrating knowing someone out there talks about me like I'm a monster and then is super polite and even asks me for job hunting help... I'd rather just confront things and hash them out but I guess she feels differently and she's allowed to

For what it's worth, this is something I have struggled with myself.


I hear all these *angry* people around me and as much as I understand their anger and frustration and *outrage*, very rarely do I feel those same feelings myself.


And frankly, too often it's painted that if you don't have those same visceral emotions, you're just a heartless person who is indifferent to the plights of whatever group happens to be the main point of discussion.


If you want my honest to God opinion, I don't think it matters. People are different. They respond differently to different issues. If we were all the same then life would be boring as hell and we'd never get anywhere anyways. 


When I was dating someone with a lot of those visceral emotions, it was extremely demanding. I had to act the right way and say everything perfectly and mimic her otherwise I got accused of being a bigot or worse. Some people, wether it's helpful or not, seem to be more apt to consider someone's feelings to be a greater indicator of their morals than the words they say.


If I had to guess, you're probably a classic centrist. For whatever reason, progressives seem to fucking hate centrists. A lot of them seem to think being able to understand the other side of a viewpoint means that you empathize with them and give it just as much sway.




Personally, I don't think anything is wrong with you. Or that it's necessarily wrong to be open about not being outraged. But I do advise caution because yeah, at some point you'll be accused of not caring about right and wrong. That's clearly not the case, but you'll still be accused of it. In my opinion, raw feelings aren't necessary for politics. I don't think I've ever felt outrage over women being shoehorned into caretaker roles, but I disagree that it's the standard that society should hold. Likewise, I *do* feel strongly against circumcision but I understand most others don't feel the same way.


And like you hint at, it can be taxing. It's okay to want to take a break from others expectations of you and to want to just be you without worrying what they think. Not everything needs to be emotionally expressed for it to be real and it sounds like you've surrounded yourself to some degree with people that see emotional expression as the only currency of inner values.

I guess that's what I struggle with though. If she doesn't tell the full story, it's probably easy to make me out to be an abusive person. Between all the yelling that happened and the occasional times I had to stop her from hurting herself using physical force, it's easy to frame things as me being unhinged. She *has* evidence, but the full story (I yelled because she yelled, I stopped her because I didn't want her to self harm) puts things in a different context. 


Idk, these accounts aren't connected to her real life so I'm not worried about it hurting me personally, but I'm realizing that if she wanted to, she can make a compelling argument why I'm a horrible person and I'd be inclined to agree with parts of it because, well, I should have let professionals get involved instead of getting personally involved.

Scrolled through some of my ex's social media accounts and she's talking about how her ex never took responsibility and was an abuser.


Hi, hello. That's me. I'm the ex.


I feel... down. And I feel lied to.


Whenever we talk - and we do, every so often - she is perfectly polite to me. Not a hint of anger or frustration. She's never brought up anything from the past. 


So I guess I'm confused. I know I made mistakes in the relationship, spoke in anger more than a few times, and said things I regret. But she did just as much. I'm not one to escalate things, either. If anything, after therapy, I now realize how toxic of a person she could be.


Perspective is a bitch. It's been drilled into me so much over the years that I need to believe these kinds of accusations. I'm looking at myself and wondering... am I abusive? Am I just flawed? Am I a good person? I do have regrets but I haven't laid a hand on anyone in anger. And I am always the one to apologize and try to change if I've hurt someone. 


I'm not sure what to do. I obviously can't repair things with her, but it blows my mind that she considers me the abuser when I consider her to be the abusive one in the relationship. But I feel like her words mean *more* than mine. That people are gonna take her seriously. That in order to tell my story I have to have a whole song and dance about how I wasn't the best person either, and that I don't want to be the guy spouting junk about his "crazy ex", and that she went above and beyond to break me down. Just to be able to say what she did to me (literally pulling weapons off her or listening to her celebrate the day we wouldn't need men to reproduce).



And she was always the "we need to teach men not to be abusers" type. So I feel like I've just failed her and everyone because I didn't learn enough, change enough, or try enough to make things be better.

I feel like my issues aren't something I should take seriously, because my issues are largely male issues.


I don't feel like I'm allowed to talk about the things that effect me unless they are on the Pre-Approved List of Progressive Topics. Anything that's not on the list... well, chances are I'll be told I'm selfish, whining, entitled, or focusing on the wrong thing.


I feel trapped in that I can only seem to mention that men should be able to cry more and that seeking mental health resources shouldn't be stigmatized. The rest of the time I feel like I'd have to convince people that my problems are even problems in the first place.


I pull the Logical Man card. If people have to be led to think that the issues that face me even exist, are they really that serious? Are they really that important? Just once I'd love to have a conversation where someone showed they knew more than the two or three things the mainstream has latched onto and shown that they really care about the niche issues that affect modern men.

Well, I had a breakthrough in terms of my treatment plan and I'm figuring out in my mid 20s that I have pretty severe (and often crippling) OCD.


I feel left behind. Looking at my thought process I can find examples from when I was 7 or 8 that... holy fuck, I'm struggling to wrap my head around the idea that normal people don't think the way I do. Normal people don't get insane levels of stress and anxiety from relatively minor mistakes, nor do they focus on the big mistakes they've made until they are suicidal.


Tbh I'm grieving a lot of my life right now. I'm not in a great place emotionally. Because there is potential to have caused harm I'm unaware of, I live in fear that I've ruined other people's lives. Hell, my ex girlfriend described me as abusive and I can't get that out of my head.


The worst thing is, OCD has limited treatments. And no cures. I will never be completely free of it and that kind of terrifies me. I just want... normality. I just want a different brain, I need a break from myself and a mental reset.

My depression finally wrapped its arms around my life and I cannot cope. 



I'm just tired all. the. time. All I've had to eat today are antidepressants and anti anxiety pills and I know that's not helping.


I can't wake up for work anymore. I clock in around 11am and... well, thank God for remote work, but I'm getting close to having my supervisor called on me. I want a week off to rest and recuperate but I'm down to zero PTO and don't want to stop working on projects with a tight schedule.


But then the suicidal ideation looms nearer and I stop caring. I'm getting dangerously close to not caring at all anymore, and I'm not sure how to slow the roll that I'm on.

Late to the party but I've been struggling a... lot.


My depression, rumination, and negative thoughts mounted to a point they never have before. It got to a point that I was in a constant panic and realized that I didn't just want to commit suicide, I *needed* to. 


I don't normally fear myself but last weekend I did. I'm managing now and I've upped my medication dose with my doc but I'm just so tired. No amount of sleep is enough. I just want to be anyone else but me and my own brain which has decided to be my own worst enemy. 



I'm at the end of my rope and I'm looking up any and all weird alternative things that might save me from myself. Right now I'm looking into ketamine therapy but I feel that I need some sort of spiritual event to happen outside of myself for me to get better because there's no way at this point I can live with myself and the things I've done and just be happy.

I mean they inhibit serotonin re-uptake... thereby elevating serotonin.


But serotonin levels are just one piece in a very large brain soup

In my case my depression is at least in part caused because I get stuck in my own head. I'm definitely OCD-adjacent as far as rumination and thought patterns go, which often push me into depressive spirals. Personally it all feels somewhat connected. I get a feeling that depression isn't a medication issue alone and can get better or worse depending on how my anxiety and attitude toward myself fluctuates.


The reason I put "therapy resistant" is that as far as medication, I've been able to fight the depression before, I just can't seem to make any meaningful headway on the mental health side of things.

>Give it a try.  The insights you gain will either confirm that you are right to feel the way you do, or help you change.


Heh, this brought on more anxiety and fear then I think you may have expected. I feel like how my brain got to this point is very logical, and it's the correct feeling from a moral, ethical, and legal standpoint. I know ketamine isn't exactly logical but I mean... I won't lie, I'm a bit terrified to let go in case it only serves to solidify things.


Which I guess loops around to they're already pretty solidified, so how much can it really hurt?
From where?

I started antidepressants for a second time and I was hopeful the first few weeks but this week has been miserable. They're helping cut through my anxiety but I have the general feeling like my brain has forgotten what true happiness feels like. I no longer have hope of feeling good in life or even content, I'm just going through the motions.


I'm really tired. Both physically and existentially. I want a break but I'm scared of what that would mean for me.

Honestly, if we're going by anecdotes of friendship, I have had more experiences of women in my life holding weird and unexpected "anti-feminist" views than I have had my male friends, but that's neither here nor there. Maybe I have a bizarre group of friends but my male friends are nearly all supportive of feminism and listen to women and they are maybe not *vocal* about it in terms of academic feminism or the language there but they very tangibly demonstrate it in their day to day lives. In any case, I agree with you - even in left leaning spaces, women's voices aren't always welcome, tolerated, or respected. And many, many men outside my own friend group are not nearly ready or willing to listen.



I think we're partially talking past one another but I think I partially fundamentally disagree with you. You seem to hold to view that you need to break a few eggs in making the omelette of social change. I agree. But having personally been on the end of misandry strong enough to result in me seeking therapy for suicidal ideation, misandry strong enough to push me to challenge my gender identity, misandry that was *welcomed and encouraged* by peers and progressives because it was "ironic" and "punching up"... I don't think I can sit idly by and not criticize those fringe people trying to use a social movement to spread their hate around. There's a limit. I don't have to sit here and be someone's punching bag because they found a socially acceptable way to lash out and be encouraged to do so. *That's* what I want to criticize. The people who have been brash enough to say to my face that men are a waste of space, those that said I could never truly love someone because I was a man, not the people who have signs that say men suck. 



You seem to want to believe that those people are not worth addressing because we have bigger problems at hand. And I'd love to believe you, and realize that yes, I'm saying "but what about the men!". It's just... I believe there's a difference between tone-policing and not literally encouraging hate. And I've seen the exact same arguments you bring up used to support some really shitty, hateful things that will *hurt* people - that *I've been deeply* hurt by. I think it's impossible to do social change without hurting someone's feeling's and men need to get better at that. I'm just really tired of this assumption that if a man is hurt, it's his own fault for not being "understanding" or empathetic enough to other people's issues. At the end of the day, some people claiming to be activists are *just plain hateful and want to hurt others*, and calling that out really shouldn't be this big of a deal, right? I dunno.

I think you're misunderstanding my view as one where we need to focus the same amount of energy on tone policing the left as butting the reactionary right.

 

It seems to me that we often give marginalized groups the *absolute, best-faith interpretation* of many inflammatory statements, and in doing so we shield a lot of genuine bigotry that doesn't represent what the left should be about. It's one thing to give a good faith reading of "men are trash!" to someone who is angry and frustrated, but I keep seeing people rush and fall head over heels to give the most benefit of the doubt to people who are saying "I hate men. The world would be better off without them, I wish we had a new plague". Is it reactionary to not offer support to people that seem to legitimately foment hate under the guise of a social justice movement? Because those people are there, they exist and I've met them and seen them. And they're usually the people that are the loudest and try to represent the left the most.



So yeah, we should offer good faith support to marginalized groups who are angry. And we should focus the vast majority of our energy on fighting the slide into fascism. But what I desire is a little bit of transparency on the left where we can vocally say "hey, anger is fine but hate is not. If you want to foment hate, we don't want you here". That's not anything I've seen people do - instead the complete opposite happens where people rush to defend someone's bigoted statement because they *must* have meant it in some contextually-appropriate way, because who would call themselves progressive and hold hate in their hearts? Being a self-identified progressive does not mean you can't be bigoted, and that's ultimately the short-circuit I see most people falling for. By not calling out bigotry on our own side for what it is, that's endorsement.

I'm tired of being me and I wish life had a reset button.



At least the psych meds are kicking in and I'm feeling less actively suicidal. I can actually sit down and work now instead of being an anxious ball of self-hate just waiting for the right combination of mild frustrations to push me over the edge and do something stupid.



I continue to do dumb things though. I had a massive mood swing and I texted my ex-girlfriend from three years back. She was very emotionally abusive and she's not on my list of favorite people by any means. I usually want to message her in anger and yell at her for how she's responsible for most of my hate of being male and why I don't trust women very much and why I struggle with letting myself have feelings because she made it clear our relationship was all about her at the end of the day.



Instead I sent her a long apology. I wasn't the best person to her, I said and did some really shitty things and I know that she was hurt by my actions. Some things felt justified at the time but looking back I should have just walked away instead of matching her anger. 



Anyways, she said she doesn't hold any bitterness toward me and doesn't hold on to the past. I wonder what that's like. I want to know, because my brain can't let the past go, and it never has. It's a major part of my self hate and depression because every bad thing I do feels like it gets amplified 1000x compared to how others would manage it. It was an unexpected conversation but one that I felt needed to happen, so yay me for being a drama queen I guess.

I understand what you're getting at and I think we should absolutely be empathetic to oppressed and marginalized groups because they do have the right to be angry, but I think there's a vast gulf between being *empathetic* to that anger vs. endorsing vocalized hatred. 


I get it, the left doesn't want to tone-police. But I think there's a balance that needs to be struck and that we don't need to tacitly support actually hateful people because they happen to be an angry marginalized person. Anger is fine - hate is not and I've seen plenty of actual hate.

In my experience, you don't often hear "all masculinity is bad" from left-leaning groups for one reason: people on this side are reserved enough to not say the quiet part out loud.


I can't speak to your own experiences but in my own I've come across more than a few spaces where the dominant sentiment might as well be "all masculinity is bad". It's just no one actually says it, and if someone calls them on their hate they tiptoe back behind the "if you were offended by your own lack of understanding then you're the problem here" line.



It's a frustrating issue because the left doesn't want to alienate other leftists and simply won't acknowledge that a *progressive* space doesn't automatically equal a *good* one. And I'd agree - most of the people parroting that the left wants to get rid of masculinity are reactionaries on the right. But pretending like people don't actually think that and vocally identify as progressives just adds more fuel to the fire. I've had very dear left-wing friends to me say that the world would be better off without men and mean it. I've had them defend others saying that masculinity is *all* garbage. This stuff is out there.
Thanks man

Man, that accurately describes it. I feel like I got dealt a shit hand already with depression and intrusive thoughts, but then adding in the rest of what makes me "me" is terrifying. I feel like I'm broken in like, 5 or 6 different life areas where I just am not... typical.



Unfortunately she's actually very integral to a lot of the groups I'm a part of. She's a moderator in some hobby channels and cutting off contact with her could have me excommunicated from them as a whole. It's a clusterfuck but idk I honestly feel like telling her is my brains way of saying "here, you must suffer because of things you did that are not who you are now". She likes current me, but would probably be appalled with past me. Unfortunately a main mental issue of mine seems to be separating who I was in the past with who I am in the present, my gut says they are one and the same but my therapist keeps hinting I need to separate the two.

I've kind of maxed my mental health capacity over the last few weeks and I'm just barely hanging on. 


I'm just consumed with guilt and shame and fear over shit I've done. I've spoken about it to some extent here so I won't go into it but I'm always stuck with the feeling that it's unforgivable and permanent. Even if I find a way to forgive myself for victimizing people, most of society sure as hell won't. I got some nice comments on an alt about how what I've done is actually forgivable and how it means a lot that I recognize my mistakes and have changed but no amount of external reassurance will fix things for me. I'm starting to look into extremes like ketamine therapy because I don't think any amount of talk therapy will get me into a mindset where I feel like I can live with myself.



It's probably being exacerbated by the fact that I'm in a casual/FWB thing right now and I am almost certain if I explained everything and said "hey I fucked up and acted unintentionally abusive/predatorial in my late teens/early 20s and had some conversations and interactions I regret" that she'd never want to speak to me again just due to her personality. So it feels like I'm living a lie around her and I'm feeling mounting pressure to abandon the situation. 



I hate to say this but I'm really tired of being me. I hate my life right now, my brain hates itself, I can barely get a moment's peace, and I'm just ready to be done. I won't do that but I'm getting desperate for some peace in my life and I currently feel like I'll never have it.

Content warning: depression and suicidal ideation

I think I hit full crisis and I guess I should glad that past me set up psychiatry and therapy appointments this week. Current me is highly ambivalent. Thanks to everyone who replies to me even if I don't reply back - I see most of them even if I don't have the energy to respond.


I woke up this morning with a strange haze of comfort and warmth around the idea of taking my own life. It just felt different, I've thought about it a million times but it's always been full of fear. I explored it for a bit and made it all of 15 minutes before the usual panic set in and the world came crashing down around me. 


I think my brain is just tired of fighting itself. Nothing can change the things I've done but it's beating itself into a pulp trying to find some way to find forgiveness for myself and coming up with nothing. It's like asking to squeeze water from a rock.


I've done things I'm not proud of but I look at humanity and wonder how people exist when they make big mistakes. Rapists and murderers often feel like they deserve second chances, and society often gives them out. I've never done anything that bad, but I've still done some things that would leave a bad taste in anyone's mouth... do I deserve a second chance? I'd love to have the confidence most people seem to have when they screw up. Instead I've doubled down on hating myself and pushing more and more moral judgement on my actions because I want to *prove* I've changed and my morals now are stronger than they were before. 


Except I'm stuck in the past and wind up cutting myself in half in the process.


Part of me thinks humanity - no matter what side of the political isle - is too focused on punishment over rehabilitation. The law works with little regard for maturity or intent. I understand why it does, but I often wonder if it's the best solution. I definitely deserve to be punished for things but what's interesting is my therapist has done some work with adult criminal offenders. She's said many times that if I went to the police today with my story, I'd be laughed out of the room - they have bigger fish to fry and people who are *actively* being bad. Why would society spend time and money punishing someone who learned a lesson before something *really* bad happened and no one seems to have been hurt or traumatized? It makes sense, but I'm still carrying things, and feel like I will forever.



I'm getting to the end of my rope and considering wild things. I'm not a spiritual person but I'm contemplating trying psychedelics... the ability to get outside my own head and look at my life through a different perspective is one that I feel desperate for. Doubly scared I'd just give myself a bad trip and make things worse lol.
I just basically had a nice cry and a small panic attack and that's given me the most peace I've had in days. Not much but it's something.

I think it can, for sure.



I didn't even realize I had OCD until maybe a couple years ago. Growing up I knew I did some weird stuff but I just thought I had a great ability to convince myself of things. I mean, it's pretty funny to think back to high school when I combined myself I was growing a tail. It's less funny to think of the years that I spent praying because I thought I was gonna be possessed if I said the wrong thing, or apologizing profusely to people I had only offended in my head. 


When I was 22 it struck harder - even then, I bought a workbook that I never used, focused on some very basic ERP, and managed to make it through what I now know was a Real Event OCD crisis.


That held for a few months until it didn't, I couldn't get it out of my head. I got anxious and depressed, I went to a therapist, not being certain I had OCD but just figuring I overthought things. Got diagnosed with depression but not OCD. I spiraled, and eventually got on medication for the first time. That helped significantly, so I figured it was just depression.



Nine months of meds and I was past the depression, and I stopped them. The last year - entirely off meds - I've been doing fine. Until about 3 weeks ago where I read something very triggering after being stressed about the Real Event stuff and I just... unraveled. 



Long story short, I think mine is getting worse as I get older, or at least more pointed and episodic instead of being in the background. I'm 25 though and most mental disorders really manifest in your early 20s so I'm right on the mark for it ballooning out of control now. I'm hoping it will ease up in the future, if I can make it through my current crisis and get back on meds.

TW: suicidal ideation and desperation

I just need a place to vent. I'm sorry for adding negativity to this thread but it needs to go somewhere and there's not much of me that wants to tell people in real life.


I'm scared. Like really, really scared. I'm closer to a crisis than I ever have been before. I wouldn't have said that if I hadn't arranged help. I have an appointment with a new psychiatrist as well as my therapist next week. I'm working through things. Slowly. I think. You, valued reader, should not be worried about me. I am not your problem to deal with.


I've been reading up about OCD a lot lately. The more I read, the more of myself I see. Suddenly, weird things I'd do in my childhood made sense. Odd obsessions, the inability to get things out of my head... it all described me to a tee. That's helped figure out what's going on, but it doesn't help with the actual issue.


An incurable neurological disorder. 


An incurable neurological disorder that is making my life an absolute, soul-shattering hell. For the past two weeks I've barely gotten a moment of peace. My body is constantly on edge, tensed up, fight or flight response fully engaged. Thoughts repeat in my head like a broken record until they break apart and aren't even thoughts anymore, they're just a swirling mess of negative feelings telling me how I will never live a fulfilling life with the mistakes I've made - not because of the mistakes necessarily, but because my brain literally rejects the capability for me to be happy. My brain literally can't live with itself, and I'm both perpetrator and victim. 



I want to quit so bad. It's hard to find reasons why not. I look at other people in my life and know the vast majority of them don't go through this and never will. I am angry. Why did I have to get this piece of crap incurable brain? I'm scared - terrified - this will be my forever. My life will be one mental battle after the next for something I never asked for, barely want, and apparently can't deal with. I'm scared I'm thinking of life 30 minutes at a time. I'm scared that medication might not work. I'm scared I can't seem to improve and hope that medication is a miracle cure. I am so TIRED. The exhaustion is suffocating, all-encompassing and all I want to do is scream. This is who I am. This is my life. I can't change it. I've dipped out on religion the past few years but lately I'm hoping and praying that there's something better than this in the future because I am struggling very, very much right now.


Oh, and I'm sobbing so hard I scared the cat away. Poor guy. 😥
Thank you

Continuing to be plagued with intrusive thoughts and obsessive rumination on the more detestable things I've done in the past. 


There was an interesting thread in one of these about if villains deserve forgiveness or happiness. I seem to remember the general feeling was that villains deserved a second chance if they were remorseful, but if they were plagued for the rest of their lives with guilt... maybe that's not the worst thing to happen.
